description: Machine-readable inventory of accessibility audit checks for validation and generated maps.

statusTaxonomy.present: The expected invariant is fully satisfied.
statusTaxonomy.partial: Most signals resolve, with a small number of exceptions, or the codebase shows mixed adherence.
statusTaxonomy.violation: Concrete markup or configuration breaks the invariant.

enrichmentFlags.description: Restrict reporting to error-level accessibility findings.

relatedAudits.relationship: Owns the eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y configuration this audit expects.

checks.title: jsx-accessibility lint plugin
checks.expectation: eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y is installed and the recommended or strict ruleset is enabled in the active ESLint configuration.
checks.violationSignal: The plugin is missing, the recommended set is not extended, or the plugin is disabled at file or directory level.

checks.title: Axe in development
checks.expectation: @axe-core/react is initialised in development mode so violations are logged to the browser console during local work.
checks.violationSignal: The dependency is missing, or no entry point imports it behind a development guard.

checks.title: Component-test integration
checks.expectation: jest-axe or vitest-axe is available and at least one component test asserts toHaveNoViolations.
checks.violationSignal: The matcher dependency is missing, or no test file uses it.

checks.title: End-to-end accessibility scan
checks.expectation: @axe-core/playwright or the Cypress equivalent is configured and at least one end-to-end spec runs an axe scan against a rendered page.
checks.violationSignal: The scanner dependency is missing, or no spec invokes it.

checks.title: Storybook accessibility addon
checks.expectation: When Storybook is in use, @storybook/addon-a11y is registered.
checks.violationSignal: The Storybook configuration does not list the addon.

checks.title: Continuous integration enforcement
checks.expectation: A continuous-integration step runs the unit and end-to-end accessibility checks and fails the build on violations.
checks.violationSignal: No workflow step invokes the relevant accessibility test command.

checks.title: Semantic HTML over generic containers
checks.expectation: Interactive elements use the right tag and list-shaped UI uses list elements.
checks.violationSignal: A div or span with an onClick and no role, keyboard handler, or tabIndex; a list rendered with div children; a clickable item that should be a button or anchor.

checks.title: ARIA used correctly
checks.expectation: ARIA attributes appear only on supporting elements, are not redundant, and are present where required.
checks.violationSignal: ARIA on an element where it has no effect, redundant ARIA, icon-only buttons without an accessible name, disclosure triggers without aria-expanded, or modals without aria-modal and a labelling strategy.

checks.title: Keyboard support
checks.expectation: Every interactive element is reachable by Tab and operable by keyboard, and focus is visible.
checks.violationSignal: outline: none without a replacement focus style, custom widgets that skip the authoring-practices keyboard model, or keydown handlers that block default behaviour without re-implementing it.

checks.title: Focus management
checks.expectation: Modals trap focus and restore on close, route changes move focus to a sensible target, and a skip-to-content link is the first focusable element.
checks.violationSignal: A modal without focus trap and restoration, a custom router with no focus handling, or auto-focus on load on a non-form-first page.

checks.title: Forms
checks.expectation: Every input has an associated label, errors are programmatically associated with fields, required fields are indicated for both screen readers and sighted users, and grouped controls use fieldset and legend.
checks.violationSignal: An input whose only label is a placeholder, an error not tied to its field by aria-describedby, a required field marked only with an asterisk, or a radio or checkbox group without fieldset and legend.

checks.title: Images and media
checks.expectation: Every img has an alt attribute, content SVG icons have an accessible name, videos have captions, and auto-playing media is muted with a pause control.
checks.violationSignal: img without alt, a content SVG with no accessible name, or video autoplay without muted and a pause control.

checks.title: Colour and contrast
checks.expectation: Text colours meet WCAG AA contrast against their backgrounds and information is never conveyed by colour alone.
checks.violationSignal: Statically-defined text and background pairings below 4.5:1 (or 3:1 for large text), or UI states differentiated only by colour.

checks.title: Motion and animation
checks.expectation: Long animations respect prefers-reduced-motion and no essential information is delivered through animation alone.
checks.violationSignal: Animations longer than five seconds with no pause control, global stylesheets with no prefers-reduced-motion block, or auto-rotating carousels without pause.

checks.title: Text and content structure
checks.expectation: Headings are in document order with no skipped levels and link text is descriptive in isolation.
checks.violationSignal: A page that skips heading levels, multiple h1 per page outside a warranted context, or non-descriptive link text.

checks.title: Document language
checks.expectation: The HTML shell sets html lang to a real language code.
checks.violationSignal: The HTML shell does not set a non-empty lang.

checks.title: Per-route document titles
checks.expectation: The document title updates on every navigation using the framework's title primitive.
checks.violationSignal: Routed views do not update the document title.

checks.title: Skip-to-content link
checks.expectation: A skip link to the main landmark exists and is the first focusable element on every page.
checks.violationSignal: No visible-on-focus skip link is rendered in the application shell.

checks.title: Route announcement
checks.expectation: Client-side navigations are announced to assistive technology.
checks.violationSignal: No live region or framework-provided announcer handles route changes.

checks.title: Viewport meta
checks.expectation: The viewport meta tag is present and does not disable scaling.
checks.violationSignal: The viewport meta is missing, or sets user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1.

checks.title: Landmark roles
checks.expectation: The application shell renders the standard landmarks once per page, with navigation and complementary where the design has them.
checks.violationSignal: Duplicate landmarks of the same role without a differentiating aria-label, or missing core landmarks.

checks.title: Error and not-found pages
checks.expectation: Custom error and 404 pages have a heading, manage focus, and offer a way back to the main application.
checks.violationSignal: An error or not-found route without a heading or without a link back to a known landing route.

checks.title: Authentication pages
checks.expectation: Sign-in and sign-up forms support password-manager autofill, declare input purposes, and do not trap users in modal flows that break with a screen reader.
checks.violationSignal: Inputs use the wrong autoComplete values, or forms are nested inside non-dismissible modals.
